mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES from t-1w to t-0w signals more commuting and weekday trip chaining. That should lift retail and recreation visits within four weeks because workers add discretionary stops after work.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays above its recent low but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply depressed, people substitute local discretionary trips for long commutes, raising nearby retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -55 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -55 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in PARKS mobility below its prior three-week level marks a pullback in outdoor discretionary activity that spills over into fewer retail-and-recreation trips one week later.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week after being above -20
failure_condition: If PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week after a less negative baseline and RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates easing access constraints and denser daytime activity, which should feed through to higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points while WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points over two weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rise by at least 5 points over two weeks but RETAIL_REC is not higher than its previous 4-week mean over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM while RETAIL_REC stays weak captures a substitution toward essentials and away from discretionary outings. That pattern predicts lower retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above its recent mean while RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL begins to fall from an elevated level, part of the home-based activity mix shifts back outdoors, and retail-and-recreation mobility improves within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops by at least 2 points from a level above +8
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops by at least 2 points from above +8 and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT combined with a smaller-than-usual PARKS decline indicates broader mobility normalization rather than isolated commuting, which should raise retail-and-recreation visits over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves while PARKS does not fall more than 5 points from its prior week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves and PARKS is stable or only slightly lower, but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average over the next month, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained stabilization of PARKS after a sharp drop signals that weather-sensitive discretionary activity has bottomed out. Once that floor is reached, retail and recreation mobility should stop weakening and turn higher within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stops falling and holds within 3 points of the prior week after a drop below -30
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes near a recent low but RETAIL_REC keeps declining in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.
